messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — Dedicated pool ded-zeppelin-1: GPU node gpu-17 reported repeated driver OOM and process evictions (detected 3177701200). Potential tenant impact: high latencies and 503s for Zeppelin Health VPC tenants. paging: @maya (oncall-sre) @ajay (platform-eng) :rotating_light:

maya (oncall-sre): seeing it. acked. grabbing logs and current routing state.

ajay (platform-eng): i'm on network traces + scheduler. quick ask: is this a hardware ECC spike or a workload-driven memory exhaustion?

carmen (customer-ops): flagged to customer success and account rep. Carmen to draft ASAP customer note once we have impact summary.

maya (oncall-sre): initial metrics: GPU mem usage jumps to 98% then driver OOM, qemu/container killed causing session loss. Multiple tenants reported tail-latency spikes. Not seeing host thermal alarms. Looks like a leaking workload + sustained long-context KV cache allocations.

maya (oncall-sre): mitigation plan: 1) isolate affected node from serving 2) drain running containers/tenants with graceful switchover 3) if drain fails, force-evict 4) promote standby capacity in ded-zeppelin-2 pool 5) open HW ticket if persistent.

ajay (platform-eng): agree. I'm going to initiate tenant isolation and re-route policy. Running drain command now.

maya (oncall-sre): paste of drain command and expected output:
```
# rictl (redwood-inference internal) node drain
rictl node drain --node gpu-17 --pool ded-zeppelin-1 --grace-period 30s --reassign-tenant-policy promote-standby
# expected: tenants cordoned, new connections routed to ded-zeppelin-2
```

incident-bot: ACTION — drain initiated by ajay at 3177701800. Status: cordon-ok, migration-started.

support-bot: NOTE — Customer-facing incident channel created: #incident-zeppelin-3177701234 (private). Carmen added.

maya (oncall-sre): migration progressing. Seeing kv-cache eviction step for long-lived sessions. One tenant (user-tenant-7) failed graceful migration due to in-progress large generation job — caused backend process to die and restart; transient 503s logged.

ajay (platform-eng): forcing eviction for that tenant to unblock node. Command: `rictl tenant evict --tenant user-tenant-7 --force --drop-kvcache`

jordy (hw-eng): can you capture dmesg / driver log before we reboot? If it's ECC we need to escalate to hardware immediately.

maya (oncall-sre): copying logs:
```
[3177701605] nvdriver: RTXX-6300 driver: oom_kill_process: pid=4821, name=llm-worker
[3177701608] nvdriver: gpu_mem_fault: no ECC flags
[3177701610] container: oom killed pid=4821 exit=137
```

jordy (hw-eng): looks like classic allocation OOM, not ECC. I'll still schedule node replacement to be safe but treat as workload-driven mem leak for now.

maya (oncall-sre): migration completed for 95% tenants. Two tenants showed degraded step-down times >60s; logged and routed to standby pool. Latency normalized for others.

carmen (customer-ops): customer comms draft (internal): "Hi Zeppelin team — we detected a GPU node instability in your dedicated pool ded-zeppelin-1 which caused brief 503s for some in-flight requests. We've migrated tenants to warm standby capacity and are continuing to investigate. We'll follow up within 2 hours with root cause and timeline for node replacement." OK to send?

maya (oncall-sre): yes send. Add that we've avoided data loss and sessions were re-routed; include mitigation steps.

ajay (platform-eng): scheduling autoscale to warm additional standby capacity for the pool to avoid future failure window. Also adding a temporary per-tenant max-concurrent-generation cap for ded-zeppelin-1 to limit memory churn:
```
# temporary policy
rictl pool patch ded-zeppelin-1 --policy "max_concurrent_generations=4,kvcache_eviction=aggressive"
```

incident-bot: UPDATE — pool policy patched at 3177705500. Autoscale triggered +2 nodes to warm standby.

jordy (hw-eng): opening HW ticket HWT-2026-588 for replacement of gpu-17 (firmware snapshot taken). ETA for on-site swap: 12-18 hours.

maya (oncall-sre): while we wait for hardware: 1) keep node cordoned 2) keep aggressive kvcache eviction policy 3) monitor per-tenant error budget and rollback policy if errors > 1% over 10m.

support-bot: ACTION — Monitoring alert threshold created for ded-zeppelin-1: tenant error-rate >1% triggers rollback to standby routing.

carmen (customer-ops): sent to customer at 3177707200. Customer responded: "Thanks — please confirm if any long-running jobs were interrupted and if we'll need to restart them."

maya (oncall-sre): replied to customer: "We saw a handful of long generations that were restarted automatically; no persistent state lost. If you have annotated long-running jobs, please surface them and we'll coordinate restarts."

ajay (platform-eng): follow-up: adding a short-term guard in the scheduler to prefer preemption of high-memory jobs on pools with warm-standby available. Will monitor perf impact.

jordy (hw-eng): hw-note: on extraction we found slight VRM instability; replacement part ordered. We'll replace during maintenance window unless node shows further regression — then we will hot-swap immediately.

maya (oncall-sre): summary for post-incident: root cause likely runaway memory allocations in a tenant workload that pinned GPU memory leading to driver OOMs and container kills; mitigations were tenant isolation, forced evictions, autoscale and policy hardening. Hardware replacement scheduled as precaution.

carmen (customer-ops): action items: 1) send incident recap to Zeppelin with timeline and mitigations 2) offer engineers for restart coordination 3) include follow-up RCA after HW replacement and workload analysis.

maya (oncall-sre): I'll start the incident timeline doc and collect traces. tagging @ajay @jordy for postmortem owners for platform and hardware respectively.

incident-bot: INCIDENT — ded-zeppelin-1 degraded -> mitigated at 3177718600. Incident severity lowered to S2.

maya (oncall-sre): leaving follow-up monitoring on overnight. anyone else?

ajay (platform-eng): i'll monitor autoscale and scheduler changes for 4 hours.

jordy (hw-eng): i'll track replacement and firmware checks.

carmen (customer-ops): i'll schedule customer follow-up for tomorrow 10:00 PT.

support-bot: CLOSING NOTES: thread archived to incident DB under id INC-2026-2279.

maya (oncall-sre): thanks team. moving to postmortem draft. :white_check_mark:
